topic: Nepal Election: RSP's Victory and Implications for India

subtopics.title: Nepal's Political System and Parties
subtopics.summary: Nepal is a Federal Democratic Republic with a multi-party system under its 2015 Constitution. Its Parliament is bicameral, and the House of Representatives combines FPTP and PR seats. Political instability is a long-standing feature, and no government has completed a full term since the restoration of democracy in 1990.
facts: The Constitution of Nepal was adopted in 2015.
Nepal is a Federal Democratic Republic with a multi-party system.
The President is the ceremonial head of state; the Prime Minister is head of government.
Parliament is bicameral: House of Representatives and National Assembly.
FPTP: candidate with the highest votes wins. PR: seats allocated by party vote share.
The 275-member House of Representatives has 165 FPTP seats and 110 PR seats.
No government has completed a full term since the restoration of democracy in 1990.
Nepali Congress was founded in 1947, CPN-UML in 1991 and CPN-Maoist Centre in 1994.
KP Sharma Oli, CPN-UML leader, has served as Prime Minister for the 4th time since 2015.
Oli succeeded Pushpa Kamal Dahal (Prachanda), who had been Prime Minister since 2009.

subtopics.title: Challenges and Gains for India
subtopics.summary: Shah's assertive nationalism could harden Nepal's stance on the Kalapani-Limpiyadhura dispute and the 1950 Treaty. The decline of traditional parties means New Delhi must rebuild its diplomatic networks. A stable single-party majority and technocratic governance could align with India's Neighbourhood First Policy.
facts: The Kalapani-Limpiyadhura dispute could harden Nepal's stance under Shah's assertive nationalism.
RSP proposes revisiting the 1950 India-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship.
Revisiting the treaty could reduce India's traditional diplomatic leverage in Kathmandu.
Nepal's effort to reduce dependence on India may redirect trade and connectivity projects toward others, including China.
Decline of traditional parties requires New Delhi to rebuild diplomatic networks beyond long-standing channels.
A single-party majority government could provide a stable environment for long-term policy.
RSP's technocratic approach may align with India's Neighbourhood First Policy, especially cross-border rail, power grid and infrastructure.
Madhesh lies in the Terai plains of south-eastern Nepal, bordering the Indian state of Bihar.
Madhesh is often called the 'Granary of Nepal' and has demanded greater political representation.
